chapters.title: Solving what can be solved
chapters.limits: Structured problem-solving is a general skill. Legal, financial, employment, or safeguarding problems may require qualified advice beyond the scope of an introductory course.

chapters.limits: Behavioural experiments are used across CBT approaches. This lesson illustrates the reasoning process; individual experiments may need adaptation and professional guidance.

chapters.limits: Attention practices can be useful, but persistent or intrusive thinking may require tailored support. This lesson does not establish the cause of any individual’s repetitive thoughts.

chapters.title: The rules underneath
chapters.limits: Core beliefs and assumptions are formulation concepts, not labels to impose on someone. Deeply distressing beliefs may be better explored with a qualified practitioner.

chapters.title: Working with a complicated situation
chapters.limits: The fictional workplace example teaches tool selection, not employment advice. Practical and professional support may be essential; no outcome is guaranteed.
